extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A benchmark of 11.5K college-level multimodal questions across 30 subjects and 6 disciplines for evaluating expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was manually curated in three stages: selecting subjects, recruiting over 50 university students including co-authors to collect multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and create new questions when needed, followed by cleaning, formatting, typo checking, and difficulty filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Potential duplicates were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity and reviewed by authors; problems were checked for format and typos; authors categorized difficulty levels and excluded about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors and specializing in relevant majors, collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and created new questions when necessary; authors later reviewed duplicates, formatting, typos, and difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Authors reviewed suspected duplicates and performed quality control, and expert annotators analyzed 150 randomly sampled GPT-4V errors to identify root causes of mispredictions.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors; 90 college senior students were involved as human experts for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by the societal importance of monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled adult labor and lead to job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that the manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI; there is no direct mapping to the 90th percentile of skilled adults, college exams are not the only relevant tasks, the manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects may be insufficient.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal models under zero-shot, few-shot, validation, and test settings; the validation set is useful for hyperparameter selection.

name.evidence: We introduce the Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning (MMMU) benchmark, a novel benchmark meticulously curated to assess the expert-level multimodal understanding capability of foundation models across a broad scope of tasks.

description.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Data Collection. Our benchmark collection takes three stages. Firstly, we go through the common university majors to decide what subjects should be included in our benchmark. In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The questions in our benchmark were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Data Quality Control. To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. We meticulously examine 150 randomly sampled error instances from GPT-4V’s predictions. These instances are analyzed by expert annotators who identify the root causes of mispredictions based on their knowledge and the golden explanations if available.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. Human Experts. We involve 90 college senior students, selected to represent a wide range of experts in the corresponding 30 subjects (3 student experts per subject).

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: To determine if an external image-to-text tool can enhance these LLMs’ performance on MMMU, we deploy OCR by MMOCR or captioning by LLaVA-1.5 to provide the recognized text information to text-only LLMs.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: AI system that reaches “at least 90th percentile of skilled adults” in a broad range of tasks, thus starting to achieve “the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor” for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MMMU, constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions.
